title: A Vulnerability Alert to Handle
context: The weekly scanner reports 214 findings, including a critical flaw on an exposed payment server and a flaw on an old unpatchable internal server. You must drive remediation in three decisions.

n1.text: 214 findings just arrived. What is the first action?

choices.text: Prioritize by severity, exposure, and asset criticality
choices.why: You do not remediate 214 findings in scanner order: context determines the work order.

choices.text: Apply all patches in the order they are listed
choices.why: Without prioritization, you risk breaking production for minor flaws.
Dismissing findings without analysis can hide a flaw exploitable in a chain.

n2.text: The internal server is end-of-life: no patch exists. What do you decide?

choices.text: Document the exception, isolate the server, apply enhanced monitoring, and get owner sign-off
choices.why: This is a compensated, time-bound risk acceptance: the only defensible response.

choices.text: Declare a false positive to lighten the report
choices.why: The flaw is real: classifying it as a false positive is falsification.

choices.text: Do nothing until a patch exists
choices.why: The lack of a patch does not eliminate the risk: you must at least contain it.

n3.text: The payment server patch is applied. How do you close the ticket?

choices.text: Rescan with the same method, verify the finding is gone, then report
choices.why: Verification by rescan is the proof of closure before reporting.

choices.text: Mark the ticket complete immediately after rebooting
choices.why: Rebooting does not prove the vulnerability is gone.

choices.text: Wait for the next annual scan to verify
choices.why: Such a long delay leaves the exposure window open.

n4.outcome: You executed the full loop: contextual prioritization, compensated risk acceptance, rescan verification, and reporting.

debrief: Prioritization combines severity, exposure, criticality, and known exploit.
An unpatchable asset requires a documented exception and a compensating control.
Without a rescan using the same method, closure is not proven.
